Well, you get that back though when you return them. All you have to do is take them off your head and hand them in.
Well, I don't like the idea of handing money over because it's like when you get a flat and that, and you put a deposit in. You never get the full deposit back. I don't like deposits.

q: Ricky said that when they all watched a bit of Brokeback Mountain, they each had different thoughts. What was Karl's explanation?
a: They were all sat in different places

s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to Medicine · 2008
ex: I sat down and we watched the same thing. We watched a bit of Brokeback Mountain, and we all have different thoughts.
Yeah, because we're all sat in different places.

No, no roughly speaking, we had the same experience when we're looking at the same thing, but it doesn't mean you assess it the same way, doesn't mean, you understand it the same way and it doesn't mean you apply the knowledge in the same…

q: Karl's mate said tea bag preference was "all in your head" and tested him with Tetley, PG Tips and Twinings. How did Karl describe the Tetley?
a: Just the one in the middle
x: Sweet, with a hint of biscuit
f: Karl picked out his favourite, Twinings English Breakfast, "straight away". His tasting notes: PG is "very strong", Twinings "quite fresh and light".
ex: Can you really tell the difference?

Yeah, I can. I've done like a little test on it because my mate was saying, oh, it's rubbish. It's all in your head. And he had a selection of tea bags. We had nothing else going on. He said, right, what I'm gonna do, I'm gonna make three…
Party time. Party time in the Pilgrim household. Oh, when was this? How old were you?

Oh, just going back a few months. I was like, it's like a Jilly Goulden, just sort of having a little. You can tell by the smell of a PG because it's strong tea that very strong. Twinings is quite fresh and light. Tetley was just the one…

q: Karl said that in the 80s everyone moaned about a lack of hospital beds. When he was in hospital with kidney stones, what was in short supply?
a: Pillows
f: Karl: "Loads of beds, not enough pillars." One had to be fetched for him: "Brought it back, was still warm." His lesson: "Don't solve problems."
ex: Yeah. Like I said that time when I was in hospital and, you know, I remember in the 80s, everyone was going, oh, there's not enough hospital beds and all that. When I was in hospital with. What's it, kidney stones.

Loads of beds, not enough pillars. So that's the way it works. It sorted out the bed problem. They give me a bed at night. I was going out and got a pillar. He had to go off and get one. Brought it back, was still warm.
Oh, that had been between a dead head.
So that's what I'm saying. It's kind of like you get all the beds. New problem. Where's the pillars? Don't solve problems.

q: Karl wasn't impressed by his work trip to Boston. According to him, what is there to see there?
a: Dunkin' Donuts and Starbucks

Baseball and a lot of chowder

ex: Uhh.. I mean, you're talking about traveling the world and you know, opening your eyes and, uhm, seeing new things- There's nothing to see in Boston. It's Dunkin' Donuts and Starbucks.
There's nothing else is there? I'm not being unfair there. I mean, it looks nice. There's nice buildings.

q: Karl's Auntie Nora once phoned his mam because she was worried about what?
a: Breaking wind that went on for five minutes

Her pills turning her tongue green
A cough that kept the neighbours up

ex: And uh, she said "Oh, how are you doing?" and that. She said "Alright." uh, "Bit worried though." and me mam said "Why, what's up?" Said "I've uh, been breaking wind." So she goes "Well, yeah." Says "No, but this one is going on and on and…
And she was like- she was- she was like, wh-what would you say? Whats- passing wind, farting for five minutes. One- one thing. Not like...you know, trumping and then nothing.

q: The expert confirmed cockroaches can live a week without a head. What did Karl think humans could do if they had that facility?
a: Go back to the family and write them a goodbye note
x: Finish their shift before going to hospital
Have one last pint down the local
Pop to the shops for a replacement

ex: Why... when it was invented, has it got that facility?... Say, if someone said to humans, "We could do that with humans and, you know, if you lose your head in some accident it gives you a bit of time to, sort of, go back to your- to your…
Write them a note. You wouldn't be able to have a chat but write 'em a note sayin', "It was me own fault and, uhh, it was nice knowin' ya."
Well that would be a nice facility, I agree. But cockroaches are great survivors, I mean, they've been around for over 300 million years, they're one of the most primitive insects.

q: What outfit did Karl plan to wear for his MTV screen test?
a: His charcoal woolly hat and his anorak

ex: So I'm thinking, uhh... I don't know, I'll probably wear me wooly hat cuz that takes some years off me.
It does, he looks about 10 with a wooly hat on.
Is it quite a cool wooly hat or has it got a bobble?
It's charcoal. I'd say it's the "in"- "in" color.

a: Filmed Lanzarote and told everyone it was Mars

Asked Judith Chalmers to review Mars
Filled in the craters on Mars first

Filmed a bit of that, right, say "here we are, this is it. Ignore the little coffee shop in the background. This is Mars." 'Cause that's what it's like, just loads of dust...

q: Karl introduced the question "What's the most expensive pub in London?" with what dig at Ricky?
a: Ricky won't know because he never pays

Ricky won't know because Steve gets the rounds in

Hang on a minute, what does that mean?
What does that mean, you want me to buy the pub? How much, that’s a million pounds sir.
You go in, according to the Time Out Guide 2001 if you went in a bought a big round, it’s a dear pub.

q: A pub forgot to charge Karl for his fish and chips, so he honestly went back the next day to pay. What did he keep quiet about?

ex: No. Do you know what? The other week, I'd had a cup of tea and some fish and chips at this pub, and they only took for one. And I went back the next day and said, oh, you didn't charge me for me fish and chips.
I paid. No, I didn't tell her about the tea, though.
I just thought, well, it's pretty good that I've gone back to pay for that. How much is a tea bag? The water's free.

q: Karl went out with a girl his mate Antony fancied. Why did Karl say Antony "had no chance"?

f: They were about eight or nine. Steve: "Yeah, cause you're such a dish." Karl: "Alright, I haven't got the looks like I used to."
ex: --of-I mean, it kind of happened because…I went out with…a girl who he fancied.
And how old- how- how old were you, how old were you now?
I think that’s out of order, going out with a mate’s girl.
Yeah, but it- she didn’t like him. He had, like, big ears an’ that. He had no chance--
Yeah, cause you’re such a dish.
No, but do you know what I mean? Alright, I haven’t got the looks like I used to.

q: When Steve said the ageing girl would need ID to buy wine at Oddbins, why did Karl think that wouldn't work?

Her mam would have to sign for it

ex: Unless she had some I.D. which would be--
A bit cruel, innit? That’s alri- I-I- That on top of all her other problems. He wouldn’t even give her a glass of--
And her I.D. wouldn’t look right cause she’s aging all the time.

q: Karl explained why 'that fella's' attempt to get something to Mars crash-landed. What did he blame?
a: It was done on Boxing Day, when nobody's concentrating

What are you talking about? What was he trying to do?
He was sending something up to Mars.

q: In Karl's story about a lazy chicken that wasn't laying eggs, what did the owner put next to its little house?

ex: And the owner of it was getting fed up because, you know, he had to feed it and that.

No eggs. Right? So he was like, "I'm sick of this." Anyway, someone told him, pop a little axe next to its little house, right? So when it comes out in the morning thinking, "I'll have another lazy day doing nothing," right? He saw this…
Up for the chop, it thought.
Next day, it laid about six eggs.

q: Karl felt sorry for the happy chickens in a supermarket advert. Why did he reckon they had it worse than a rubbish chicken?
a: They love their life but still die, while a rubbish chicken would want to go

ex: No, no, I mean, I don't mean really cruel, but I mean, like. Like, there's an advert on that that's on in the, you know, in Britain, advertising some supermarket, right? And it's saying, you know, we look at- Before, you know, we kill our…
And it's going, errr- we give it a good little house to live in. It's got straw.
Yes. Well, that's better, isn't it?

q: Faced with Ricky's riddle about identical doors to heaven and hell, what did Karl want to do instead of asking a question?
a: Feel the doors for heat
x: Sniff for smoke under the door
Wait and see who comes out first
f: Karl: "I can't just sort of have a feel of the door to see if there's any heat or anything." Next he asked if he could look through the keyhole.
ex: Because the rules are you can only ask one. There aren't actually two doors labelled heaven and hell, Karl. That's a leap of imagination here.
And I've definitely got to ans... I've got to ask them a question. I can't just sort of have a feel of the door to see if there's any heat or anything.

They're identical. You stand a few yards away. You cannot tell from the outside of these doors which Is which, they're identical. The guards are identical. But the one guarding Hell always tells a lie. And the one guarding Heaven always…
I an't look through the keyhole or anything?

q: Rejecting Ricky's logic in the riddle, Karl said the guards may be identical, but with identical twins you always get what?

ex: What, as opposed to the pure logic that Ricky's just used?
I just think- 'cause there's a lot of questions in life where you don't know the answer and you go, "do you know what? I don't like the look of him".
Yeah, but they're still...identical twins, you always get a little snidey one.

q: Steve summed up Karl's Freak of the Week message as "there's always someone worse off than you". What did Karl reply?

ex: Yeah. So what you’re saying is, you just want to get a little message out there which is that there’s always someone worse off than you.
Well there’s proof of that in this room.

q: Karl ran home to tell Suzanne something he'd learnt about Lego. Where did he say the name came from?

The name came about 'cos some kids mam... the kid was messing with the bricks and she said "Le' go of them, and come have your dinner".
It's always rubbish 'innit, when I say it...

[laughing] I love that, you give yourself restrictions in your fantasy. Sort of like, look down the obituary. I love the idea that someone getting a call: "Mister Pilkington? Uhh, hello, it's Doctor Hanrahan. Barry Sheen has just passed…

His dad had broken his hip

Just like "Oh, I should call home, there's something not right."

How does that- how do you get that? What kind of feeling is that-

Wha’ wha’ wha’ Wednesday, what ya thinking about Wednesday? Just wandering around?
Just sort of think about, you know-

q: Karl passed on his dad's theory about Princess Diana's death. Who did Karl say 'made a mint' from all the flowers sold that day?

ex: All the flowers that were sort of sold that day--
Right. What, for people to leave as a commemoration or--
Yeah, they made a, made a mint, didn’t they?
Right. So what are you saying?
So are you saying, are you saying-
Just saying, you know, makes you wonder--

q: What was Karl's simple plan to stop fat people snacking in the middle of the night?

Make fridge doors twice as heavy
Fit fridges with a loud alarm

ex: I am, of course, tell you another problem that I've worked out. It might, might make a slight difference on fat people. Don't put a light in a fridge because that's just. That's just that night when they get peckish, they can see…
That might. There might be some logic in there.

q: Karl said he keeps out of posh people's circles because it's like a different club. Which two related animals did he say you never see together?
a: The whale and the hippo

s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to The English · 2009
ex: It's all alien. It's not for me. I don't like that sort of.. uh, I try and not put myself in the same sort of circles as posh people, because it's just a different -it's like a different club isn't it? Like I said to you about young people…

q: Karl claimed a lad born without a brain could still see and hear. Where had he read about it?

In a leaflet at the doctor's
On a poster at the bus stop
f: Ricky insisted it was impossible: "the ears are just receptacles." Karl: "But that's why it was in this book, it was a book of mysteries."
ex: He can’t not have a brain. Hearing and sight… is a concept within the brain…
But that’s why it was in this book, it was a book of mysteries.

q: Asked whether history is written by the victors, what did Karl suggest?
a: Let the losers bring a book out too, and let people choose

Get a referee to check every history book

No, no, because you're not around. Well, it means very often if. If someone has conquered a nation or set up a dominance somewhere that they keep an eye on, on what goes out, what, what's, you know, propaganda or whatever or what's taught…

But it's even more significant than that because it comes down to the very, very minute pieces of information that we see in every walk of life. You know, prior to black people having their freedom when they were slaves, history or the…

I suppose you can bring out two books, you know, I mean, there's loads of books. I've brought one out. If I can get one out. Let the losers bring one out is what I mean. Just let everyone have a book and then you decide, you know, let…

q: Karl only needed to drink water before 6am, so why did his diary say he had to get up at 5:50?
a: To trick his head into thinking he'd had an extra five minutes

ex: I had shepherd's pie and peas. Suzanne made it from scratch. As nice as it was, it was annoying because making stuff from scratch means loads of pots and it's my job to do the washing up. So much as the food was nice, there was loads of…
Often late, no. Just because I needed to have water before 6 o'. Clock. They said, don't have anything after 6.
Well, get up at 5:50 then, like you were planned to. You had 5 minutes sleeping.
Take 10 minutes to have water though, does it?
Well, why did you say 5:50 in the first time?
Because then it tricks me, Ed, doesn't it? Going, oh, I had an extra five minutes.
Tricks me, Ed. Because then it tricks me, Ed.

She used to make loads of socks and she'd be bringing them in and no matter what I did, no matter how much I sort of said, look, I'm sick of your socks. She kept bringing them in all the time and they had, like, pictures on and that. I…

q: Karl once saw a bloke at Ripley's in LA whose head was on back to front. How did Karl say he'd walk if that were him?

That's more annoying, innit, than your hands?
Now then, would you walk? How would you walk? Would you be walking backwards, Carl, so that you could walk? So you're basically walking forwards?
I reckon I'd walk sideways so nobody would sort of tell the difference. It just looked like,
Oh, God. He solved it again.

Yes it was! Yes, it was bears.

q: Why did Karl think watching telly on your last day would be pointless?

Sure. Yeah. Be a waste of time
You could watch 24, couldn't you? The whole day.

q: Ricky was delighted that Karl's top two favourite films of all time were Kes and what?

I love the fact that in pole position, in positions 1 and 2, of his favourite films of all time, it's The Elephant Man and Kes.

q: What was the key difference between Karl's first telling of the blinking-head story and Nick Frost's?

In Karl's version the assistant was beheaded

ex: Right now this is how Karl told me that. Until Nick Frost explained that, Karl told like, he said, “Right, well a bloke, right he had his head cut off and as it- and it- and when his head was in the basket he went, ‘Count how many times I…
I have to say though, guys, I still don’t really understand what went on there. I really do- you both lost me.
Right the story is that a bloke who’d been found doing, um, you know.
You mean that Karl has just explained it and that was a clear version?
Cause, I still don’t know what you’re talking about Karl.
Well this bloke had his head cut off for- I don’t know, experiments against God he was a doctor in the, you know uh, in olden times.

a: Put all the furniture into one room

Get a vicar round to bless the house
Move out and leave it to the ghost

ex: So stuff was- stuff was moving around all the time and they said, “Right rather than-
Right we need a housekeeper, yeah.
-rather than having the house a mess uh, until we sort this out-
I’ve got the vicar coming round. Stop moving stuff around.
I love this. Oh yeah go on.

Captures life, doesn't he? Going on and that.
I know you're a big fan of Where's Wally as well, aren't you?

q: Who taught Karl the 'survival technique' of putting your hand through the toilet paper?

A Scout leader on a camping trip

When you're in the army, you're taught survival techniques.
And they said if you're ever caught with very little toilet paper...
(laughs) Yeah. "How did he die?" "Died of a dirty arse."

q: Ricky said Karl's head was perfectly circular in a radio-award photo. What happened when Ricky put a coin over it?

The coin rolled straight off it

I put a coin on it, and it and only the ears popped out from behind the coin, isn’t it perfectly round, isn’t it?
I mean when you’ve been saying I’ve got a round head, I was a bit like “Yeh everyone has, stop having a go."
And then I saw this picture last week, I thought “God he’s right."

ex: But me dad's, ah, really good at maths. So like, he said "how many have you got?" And he always counts his and it's like, "fifteen two fifteen four fifteen six three's- three for your hat, ones..." and all that. Do you know what I mean?
He adds it up really quick.
Right, so I was like, "right, hang on a minute." And he goes, "no, what'dya mean hang on? I mean- what- what have ya got?" I say, "oh! Forget it!"
I said, "this isn't- this isn't fun if you're gonna start getting all arse-y with me.
